items.title: LIVESTOCK-CME hogs set contract lows on big supply, weak demand
points: CHICAGO, Nov 2 (Reuters) - Chicago Mercantile Exchange lean hog futures set life-of-contract lows on Monday as plentiful supplies and weak demand continued to weigh on prices.
The market has tumbled since July because of poor cash prices for hogs and slumping wholesale pork prices, analysts said.
CME December lean hog futures ended down 0.70 cent at 58.175 cents per pound and set a contract low of 57.775 cents.
April 2027 futures also set a contract low.
US beef also still faces regulatory barriers for export to China, despite Beijing renewing export licences in May for more than 400 US beef plants.
In the US cattle market, CME December live cattle futures closed down 1.250 cents at 219.700 cents per pound and touched the lowest price since October 5.
January feeder cattle futures finished up 0.900 cent at 332.675 cents per pound after falling earlier to the lowest price since October 9.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh, triggers heavy rain; thousands evacuated, coastal areas on alert

The storm crossed the coastline near Ongole in Prakasam district at around 1am, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
Track live updates The cyclone made landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, after moving across the west-central Bay of Bengal.

items.title: TRAI mandates AI-led complaint centres, 16-hour human support
points: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has directed telecom operators and internet service providers (ISPs) to run round-the-clock complaint centres that can be handled by AI agents, while mandating human assistance for at least 16 hours a day.

It has also introduced penalties of up to ₹20 lakh per quarter per service area for improper disposal or handling of consumer disputes, under amended telecom consumer complaint redressal rules released on Monday.
For the first time, the telecom regulator has included AI-based customer care services in a binding rule under the Telecom Consumer Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026.
The rules, amended after more than a decade, were last revised on July 1, 2014.

Under the amended rules, service providers will be charged ₹1,000 for every complaint and ₹5,000 for every appeal found to have been wrongly disposed of, with penalties capped at ₹20 lakh per quarter per service area.

points: The Directorate of Medical Education terminated the services of 29 contract employees of Ernakulam Government Medical College (GMC) on Sunday (November 1), leaving their families in the lurch.
The employees, aged 60 and above, were asked to discontinue service from November.

Those whose services were terminated include nursing assistants, pharmacists and last-grade workers who had been working there since the State government took over the cooperative medical college in 2013.
In 2016, the government created 315 posts to accommodate such employees.

Harikumar A.N., a 64-year-old pharmacist whose services were also terminated, echoed her concerns.

items.title: How Potable Water Quality Impacts Crew Health & Safety
points: Dozens of miles offshore in the Gulf of Mexico, a worker turns on a shower after a 12-hour shift.
The water flows clear and strong, unremarkable in every way, just as it should be.

However, that water represents a complex network of filtration, disinfection, storage, and monitoring that provides crew members with the clean water they need to live and work at sea for weeks at a time.
Potable water systems on offshore platforms and maritime vessels are critical infrastructure that crews rely on every single day, yet they operate largely out of sight and out of mind.

These systems must transport thousands of gallons of water daily, maintain quality through unpredictable conditions, and do so in an environment where contamination can spread rapidly through confined quarters.
Hoses used for potable water must be dedicated solely for that purpose, properly capped when not in use, and disinfected if they’ve been idle for more than 14 days.

items.title: US manufacturing strengthens in October, input prices stay high
points: US manufacturing activity accelerated in October, with the ISM manufacturing PMI rising to 55.5 from 54.5 in September, beating Reuters-polled economists' expectations.

items.title: Tamil Nadu can lead in expenditure reform
points: This could establish a model for reform across India.
The reform should reduce leakage, duplication, and low-value spending while creating room for human capital, infrastructure, and technologies needed for future growth.
The State’s June 2026 White Paper shows why this is urgent.
In 2024-25, committed expenditure absorbed almost two-thirdsof revenue receipts, against 49% in Maharashtra and 45% in Karnataka and Gujarat.
Interest payments alone reached almost one quarter of revenue receipts in 2025-26, against 16% in Karnataka, 12% in Gujarat, and 10% in Maharashtra.
Capital expenditure was under 1.5% of GSDP, against 1.9% in Karnataka and Maharashtra and 2.9% in Gujarat.
Thus, Tamil Nadu has an expenditure structure more rigid and less investment-oriented than its major peers.
